solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One holds booze, Chairman Jack keeping mine back

indicators.note: back says the whole assembled string is read in the opposite direction
keeping means holding something within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Chairman Mao, the Chinese leader
J is the card abbreviation for jack
a bore is a hole drilled into the ground, as for a mine or well

explanation.surface: A chairman named Jack nurses a grudge about a mine while someone holds a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' applies to everything before it: the chairman and Jack, holding the mine, are read in reverse as one string.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeroboam is an outsize wine or champagne bottle, so it is something that holds alcohol.

clue.text: Is the reader aware of casually reported capital in US?

indicators.note: casually reported means spoken in slurred everyday speech, so the sound matters

parts.note: asking the reader if they are aware is asking d'you know

explanation.surface: A writer asks whether readers know about a casually reported US capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'd'you know' runs together into the name of a state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Juneau is the state capital of Alaska.

clue.text: Struggle being overdrawn? Pay-off needed

indicators.note: being here means existing within, so the struggle sits inside

parts.note: an overdrawn account is in the red
war is armed struggle

explanation.surface: Struggling with an overdrawn account, someone needs a pay-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is a pay-off given in return for a service or achievement.

clue.text: Criticise social worker defending wrong 'un

indicators.note: defending means surrounding and protecting, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: a bee is a worker in a social insect colony
a rat is a scoundrel or wrong 'un

explanation.surface: A social worker is criticised for defending a bad lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a council employee but a bee from a hive. A wrong 'un is British slang for a rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: To berate is to scold or tell someone off angrily.

clue.text: First-class jerk oversees a police department compound

indicators.note: oversees means sits above, so in this down answer the earlier pieces come first

parts.note: ace means excellent, first-class
a tic is an involuntary jerk
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A top-rate idiot is in charge of a police department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' suggests a fool, but it is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic acid is the chemical compound that gives vinegar its sour taste.

clue.text: Lock connected with small pressure

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: A security lock is fitted to a small pressure gauge or valve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door or canal; here it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is pressure or tension, whether physical force or mental strain.

clue.text: Uncle Sam's wastebin remains cooler under half-clipped tree

indicators.note: under puts the remaining pieces below the clipped tree in this down answer
half-clipped means cut by half, leaving the front two letters

parts.note: the word tree is taken as written, to be cut in half
ash is what remains after burning
the can is slang for prison, as is the cooler

explanation.surface: An American bin's contents chill beneath a pruned tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Sam signals an American word.
explanation.definitionFit: A trash can is the American term for a rubbish bin.

clue.text: Fancy travel document used in English terminus on cruise

indicators.note: used in says the document is placed inside the English abbreviation

parts.note: a visa is a document allowing entry to a country

indicators.note: terminus on means the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A passport stamp is used at an English port at the end of a cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to imagine.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something can mean to imagine or picture it in the mind.

clue.text: Minor work brought about by character tracking VW disorder?

parts.note: minor means small

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: op. is short for opus, a work
the letter that follows V and W in the alphabet is X

explanation.surface: A minor job on a VW car caused by some character.
explanation.walkthrough: VW is not the car maker; it is the letters V and W, which X follows in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Smallpox is an infectious viral disease, one example of an illness.

clue.text: Rock band, in one word, erratic

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run from inside one through word into erratic

explanation.surface: Someone sums up a rock band's behaviour in one word: erratic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erratic' looks like an anagram signal, but it only supplies the closing letters of the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: New Order is the Manchester group formed from the remaining members of Joy Division.

clue.text: Plant sadly receding around boundary

indicators.note: around says the reversed word wraps itself about the next piece
receding means moving back, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of sorrow, said sadly
in cricket a boundary scores four or six; six is VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A plant sadly dies back around the edge of a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket boundary is a hit to the rope, scoring four or, over it, six; here six in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvia is the sage genus, a flowering garden herb and shrub.

clue.text: Maybe part of John F. Kennedy's uniform on display

definitions.text: Maybe part of John F. Kennedy

indicators.note: on puts the uniform piece after the display piece in this across answer

parts.note: to air something is to put it on display
a team's strip is its uniform kit

explanation.surface: A US president's uniform is put on show.
explanation.walkthrough: John F. Kennedy is not the president here but the New York airport named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: JFK is a major airport, and a runway or landing strip is one part of any airfield.

clue.text: Hard to cut special slice that chippy needs?

indicators.note: to cut means slicing into the other piece, so H goes inside it
special suggests something made out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A chip-shop owner needs a special hard-to-cut slice.
explanation.walkthrough: SLICE is rearranged to CISEL and H cuts into it. 'Chippy' looks like a fish-and-chip shop; it is British slang for a carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter (chippy) uses a chisel, a bladed tool for shaping wood.

clue.text: Announced mental state with shaved head

parts.note: mental is slang for mad

indicators.note: with shaved head means losing the first letter

parts.note: a republic is a state

explanation.surface: Someone declared a mental state alongside a shaved head.
explanation.definitionFit: To have made something public is to have announced or revealed it to all.

clue.text: He painted much of group travelling with horse, mid-Ethiopia

indicators.note: much of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a caravan is a group of people travelling together, as across a desert
gee-gee is a child's word for a horse

indicators.note: mid says to take the central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A painter travels with a group on horseback through central Ethiopia.
explanation.walkthrough: CARAVAN loses its last letter; IO is the middle pair of ETHIOPIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Caravaggio was the Italian Baroque artist famous for dramatic light and shade.

clue.text: Comedian exactly right to invite comment at the end

indicators.note: to invite means to take in, so the other piece is placed inside

parts.note: quite means exactly, as in quite so
a PS is a postscript, a comment at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A comedian is exactly right to ask for audience feedback at the end of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comment at the end' is the postscript added to the foot of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A quipster is someone who makes witty remarks, a joker.

clue.text: Sloth perhaps last to remove underlying garden rubbish

indicators.note: underlying means placed beneath, so in this down answer the letter comes after

parts.note: Eden is the biblical garden
tat is cheap rubbish

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of remove

explanation.surface: Remove the rubbish lying under the garden at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' looks like laziness; it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An edentate is a mammal of the order lacking front teeth, which includes sloths and anteaters.

clue.text: Dicky safe outside to knock back ale and smoke drug

indicators.note: outside says the shuffled letters go round the other piece
dicky is British slang for faulty or shaky, so the letters are rearranged
to knock back means turning back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: ale is a beer

explanation.surface: A dodgy safe, beer downed, and drugs smoked.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky is British slang for unsound or shaky, which signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To freebase is to smoke a purified form of cocaine.

clue.text: Drew attention to 5 pence

parts.note: the answer to 5 across is STRESS, and to underline is to stress
D was the abbreviation for pence in old British money

explanation.surface: Someone highlights the cost of five pence.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' points to the answer of 5 across, STRESS, whose synonym underline is needed. D for pence comes from the Latin denarius.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise or highlight something is to have underlined it, as with a pen line under words.

clue.text: Winner taking away gold over one mile — a pushover?

indicators.note: over means placed above in this down answer
taking away means removing letters from the word

parts.note: a victor is a winner
or is heraldic gold
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A winner losing gold over a single mile is a pushover.
explanation.definitionFit: A victim is an easy target, someone readily duped or beaten.

clue.text: Park greaser creates backlash

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public park
oil is a lubricant, something that greases

explanation.surface: A greasy character in the park causes a backlash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'greaser' suggests a rocker or a slick person; here it is a lubricant.
explanation.definitionFit: Recoil is the backward kick of a gun, a backlash after firing.

clue.text: Some monsters at zoo artificial

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some monsters at the zoo are fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior substitute, imitation rather than genuine.

clue.text: Each recruiting academic institution comparatively weak

indicators.note: recruiting means taking in, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: per means each, as in two per person
uni is short for university

explanation.surface: Each university that recruits feels comparatively weak.
explanation.definitionFit: Puny means small and feeble; the comparative form describes something feebler than another.

clue.text: Possibly Christian character in Athens always collecting money

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the money goes between the other pieces

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: A Greek character in Athens is always out collecting cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Christian is Fletcher Christian, who led the mutiny on HMS Bounty, not a believer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fletcher Christian led the 1789 mutiny on the Bounty, making him an example of a rebel sailor.

clue.text: Noted Roman returning amphora, say, into shade

indicators.note: into says the reversed vessel goes inside the shade

parts.note: tan is a shade of brown

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the vessel is written backwards

parts.note: an amphora is an example of a jar

explanation.surface: A famous Roman sends back an amphora into the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Trajan was a celebrated emperor of Rome, known for his column and conquests.

clue.text: Hotel room primarily trashed during annual excess

indicators.note: during says the shuffled letters sit within the yearly abbreviation

parts.note: p.a. abbreviates per annum, meaning yearly

indicators.note: trashed means wrecked, so the letters are rearranged
primarily picks out the first letter of room

explanation.surface: A hotel room is trashed during the annual party, an excess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trashed' works only on the hotel; the room's first letter follows the shuffle, inside the per annum abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an overabundance, far more of something than is needed.

clue.text: Leaves jacket

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cannabis cigarette, rolled from the plant's leaves
second meaning: a short thick double-breasted jacket worn by sailors

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb for departing; it stands for cannabis leaves rolled into a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a marijuana joint and a sailor's heavy double-breasted coat.

clue.text: School dance, Mike assuming initial sentimentality

indicators.note: assuming the initial position means taking over the first letter's place

parts.note: the waltz is a ballroom dance
Mike is the radio alphabet word for M

explanation.surface: A school dance where a boy called Mike takes the lead is full of sentiment.
explanation.walkthrough: M takes the place of W, the first letter of WALTZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmaltz is mawkish, cloying sentiment, as in over-sweet music or film.
